what: What the undo history keeps, and what it costs in time: ^report(14)'s update of 2026-10-14/15, on the Livelit Playground's Full Body slide in a browser, copied here from 014/index.html (the update's tables) and 014/data/update-2026-10-14/. Kept = the live JS heap after 12 slider edits and two forced GCs; growth = the slope from the 4th edit to the 12th.

kept.what: History.re cuts the history to 2 states whatever the setting (a probe, not a fix)
on top of the port: the newest entry of each stack stays whole until the next is pushed
livelits with modular editors: has Andrew's compaction

cap2_note: the two runs read 284 and 284 MB, growth 4.4 and 4.2 MB per edit

times_s.what: seconds from the key press to the picture changing (undo_check.mjs), 5 runs each, median (range); compare within this table only

found: not what the browser holds: over six edits the heap grew 400 to 900 MB while listeners (609), DOM nodes (47,923, detached ones too), observers and timers stayed the same
not on #2635: the same sampled profile over four edits keeps 37.5 MB there, against 390 MB on #2597
a snapshot, at last: a probe build keeps ValueHash's memo only within one synchronous run; a snapshot after six edits completes, 2.3 GB of JSON in 75 s

two snapshots, one session: objects new between edit 3 and edit 6 (12.2 million, 257 MB); a dominator tree (29 million nodes, 4.6 s, a small C program) shows three copies of one 35 MB structure, Full Body's editor with its derived data, two of them hanging from the undo history's first two entries
confirmed by a build that always cuts the history to 2 states: 284 MB kept after 12 edits, against 1,048
